summary: This work introduces verifiable benchmark circuits that mirror application circuit structure to reduce bias in quantum error mitigation methods, achieving up to 15% fidelity improvements on 100-qubit circuits with up to 2000 entangling gates on IBM superconducting hardware. The method is applied to zero-noise extrapolation and a new variant called benchmarked-noise ZNE (bnZNE), validated on Trotterized Ising and Heisenberg simulations.
motivation: Biased quantum error mitigation methods like ZNE achieve error correction up to order $\mathcal{O}(p^m)$ but retain residual fidelity bias that limits accuracy of expectation values on NISQ devices.
method: For a given application circuit, classically verifiable benchmark circuits are constructed satisfying conditions C1–C3: matching native-gate structure, efficiently classically computable outcomes, and exact expectation value $\langle O \rangle^{\mathrm{exact}}_\mathcal{B} = 1$. Bias-mitigated estimates are obtained via $\langle O \rangle^{\mathrm{b-mit}} = \langle O \rangle^{\mathrm{QEM}}_\mathcal{A}/\langle O \rangle^{\mathrm{QEM}}_\mathcal{B}$. Two benchmark circuit generation methods are provided: hardware-agnostic (Pauli rotations, small single-qubit overhead) and IBM Heron-tailored (zero overhead, using basis gates $\{\mathrm{CZ}, R_Z(\theta), X, \sqrt{X}\}$).
result: On 100-qubit ibm_fez experiments with 1–20 Trotter layers (495–1980 CZ gates), bnZNE outperforms standard ZNE in mean fidelity and root-mean-squared error for both single-site $\langle Z_i \rangle$ observables and two-site correlations; bias-mitigated bnZNE achieves best decay-rate recovery with mean improvements of order 0.05–0.11 RMSE reduction depending on circuit depth.
